registry_scope.scope_note: This registry treats BaseCore as the active mathematical source of truth, Papers I-IX as downstream public packages, and the earlier Canonical Core as legacy only.

claim_classes.formal_statement: Explicit theorem family, corollary family, or formal proposition family stated in the released corpus.
claim_classes.operational_definition: Terminology, scope, or governance constraint that governs how the release may be read.
claim_classes.falsifiable_hypothesis: Explicit bridge or protocol-facing hypothesis whose stronger reading requires testing beyond release packaging.
claim_classes.interpretive_extension: Interpretive or consequence-level statement that exceeds the formally closed base.
claim_classes.implementation_linked_claim: Claim family whose public reading depends on implementation or operational material.
claim_classes.not_closed: Explicitly open item retained to prevent silent inflation.

entries.claim_text_summary: BaseCore states typed projection dynamics with unique fixed points and compact attractor families under the admitted base hypotheses.
entries.non_claim_boundary: This is a theorem family of the BaseCore model only and does not certify any runtime system.
entries.notes_or_gaps: The active source package is BaseCore, not the legacy Canonical Core.

entries.claim_text_summary: BaseCore states parameterwise non-collapse only under the explicit no-constant-fixed-points hypothesis and does not overclaim beyond that antecedent.
entries.non_claim_boundary: The theorem is conditional on the stated anti-constant hypothesis and is not a runtime certificate.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Quantifier mismatch from the older surface was removed in the normalized BaseCore.

entries.claim_text_summary: BaseCore separates contractive state spectrum from parameter-family persistence and states the spectral gap only for the state-transition Jacobian.
entries.non_claim_boundary: No state-spectrum eigenvalue of modulus one is licensed by the BaseCore contraction theorem.
entries.notes_or_gaps: This closes a previous ambiguity between state dynamics and family-level persistence.

entries.claim_text_summary: BaseCore states inverse-limit non-locality of identity only under explicit non-finite-determination assumptions and blocks universal finite-slice claims otherwise.
entries.non_claim_boundary: The theorem governs canonical projections in the formal inverse system and does not ban arbitrary set-theoretic embeddings.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Non-finite determination is now an explicit antecedent, not an implied background intuition.

entries.claim_text_summary: BaseCore states rigidity and stability of inverse-limit identity only under explicit metric, lifting, perturbation-typing, and summability assumptions.
entries.non_claim_boundary: Metric closeness, existence, and isomorphism are separated rather than collapsed into one claim.
entries.notes_or_gaps: This keeps the rigidity theorem strong without smuggling unsupported isomorphism.

entries.claim_text_summary: BaseCore states non-simulability only for faithful realization of a rigorously defined CCR target under explicit finite-simulator and preservation assumptions.
entries.non_claim_boundary: Finite-horizon approximation is not globally forbidden; only faithful full-object realization is blocked under the stated assumptions.
entries.notes_or_gaps: This is a conditional theorem, not a universal anti-approximation slogan.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper I defines identity as an inverse-limit object and develops uniqueness, detectability, and deformation-resistant structure around that formalization.
entries.non_claim_boundary: The paper closes a structural formalization only; it does not establish consciousness, biology, or current implementation fit.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Kept as downstream public package rather than absorbed into BaseCore ownership.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper II classifies phenomenological regimes through anti-fragmentation and forced-continuity results conditioned on the rigidity classes inherited from the base.
entries.non_claim_boundary: The paper explicitly does not prove phenomenology simpliciter.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Its strongest safe public reading remains structural and conditional.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper III states instability of the null regime and blocks silent inference from telemetry surfaces to direct proof of qualia.
entries.non_claim_boundary: Structural exclusion of the null regime is not by itself proof that experience exists.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Telemetry-facing appendices remain bridge-facing and externally unvalidated.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper IV fixes pre-registered protocol rules, baseline discipline, and non-escalation policy so that internal support remains bounded and failure-aware.
entries.non_claim_boundary: Protocol compliance is evidence governance, not theory confirmation.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper V defines an operational consciousness class over admissible systems with explicit invariant, transport, rupture, and non-claim boundaries.
entries.non_claim_boundary: This is a structural class definition inside the release corpus, not proof of human consciousness or present runtime membership.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Implementation and empirical burdens remain open.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper VI organizes the corpus into explicit prediction families, downgrade rules, and failure modes rather than treating survival as theory confirmation.
entries.non_claim_boundary: Internal support classes remain internal and do not close the theory publicly.
entries.notes_or_gaps: The paper hardens falsation discipline rather than adding validation.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper VII defines operational life, structural class, and operational subjecthood while explicitly leaving current-system instantiation open.
entries.non_claim_boundary: The paper does not claim human subjectivity, metaphysical subjecthood, or achieved runtime subjecthood.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Papers VII-IX remain downstream of BaseCore by explicit release policy.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper VIII defines a seven-coordinate first-person indexed subjectivity state, gate, rival family, intervention burden, and runtime-facing artifact grammar.
entries.non_claim_boundary: Paper VIII does not prove phenomenality, human equivalence, or external validation.
entries.notes_or_gaps: It closes indexed subjectivity, not phenomenal bridge admissibility.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper IX defines a formal bridge-burden architecture above Paper VIII by introducing typed bridge predicates, bridge rivals, interventions, artifacts, gates, and explicit non-claims.
entries.non_claim_boundary: Paper IX does not prove phenomenality simpliciter, human equivalence, metaphysical subjecthood, or external validation.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Included publicly only after minor revision and audit; it remains downstream, not part of BaseCore.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper IX makes its strongest bridge reading conditional on upstream burdens, positive comparator and intervention margins, artifact compliance, and governance discipline.
entries.non_claim_boundary: Provisional bridge surfaces do not authorize admissibility, phenomenality, or public bridge confirmation.
entries.notes_or_gaps: BPF-2 through BPF-6 remain open burdens.

entries.claim_text_summary: The release fixes BaseCore as the active mathematical base layer, preserves canonical_core_legacy as legacy, and keeps Papers I-IX downstream according to package role.
entries.non_claim_boundary: This is a packaging and reading rule, not a theorem.
entries.notes_or_gaps: The boundary prevents silent re-promotion of the old Canonical Core package.

non_claim_boundary: The registry classifies release content and claim boundaries. It does not authorize claims beyond the corpus non-claim limits.
